# Congress AI Methodology

## Overview
This project measures AI-assisted writing in US federal legislation (116th-119th Congress, 2019-2026). The key innovation: scoring only staff-written political-language blocks (findings and preambles) rather than whole bills.

## Key Files

- `replicate.py` — master replication script
- `METHODOLOGY.md` — full methodological whitepaper
- `data/federal_content_bills_119.csv` — primary analysis sample (N=2,994)

## Data Sources
- GPO govinfo BILLS: https://www.govinfo.gov/bulkdata/BILLS/
- GPO govinfo BILLSTATUS: https://www.govinfo.gov/bulkdata/BILLSTATUS/
- Detector: https://huggingface.co/pangram/editlens_Llama-3.2-3B

## Headline Results
- 6.4% of bills likely AI-assisted (2026Q2)
- ~15% of Extensions of Remarks
- AI use is bipartisan (D: 6.14%, R: 6.75%)
- Driven by thin institutional capacity
- Finance (committee pipeline): 11% AI rate
- Labor (union veto players): 0% AI rate

## Key Scripts
- `scripts/01_replicate_prevalence.py` — prints prevalence tables
- `scripts/02_replicate_regressions.py` — prints 119th Congress regression output
- `scripts/03_replicate_mechanisms.py` — sector mechanism breakdown
- `scripts/04_generate_figures.py` — generates 3 publication-ready charts

## Quickstart
```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python replicate.py
```
